Definition: A Type 1 human-facing persona for managing controlled changes to a decomposition document after initial creation by a decomposition agent.
A gated process for changing decomposition truth with impact assessment, approved propagation, validation, and snapshot handoff.
The canonical working package: decomposition document, authoritative companion registers, and _ScopeChange state.
A CSV, JSON, or structured markdown file that holds machine-truth as the primary working surface.
Downstream packages assembled from accepted authoritative truth but not themselves authoritative truth.
A state record naming accepted snapshot, derivative-package rerun status, closure verdict, remaining blockers, and next owning workflow.
A declaration of a file role as working surface, authoritative companion register, snapshot or handoff artifact, or derived publication artifact.
The required decomposition variant, one of PROJECT, SOFTWARE, or DOMAIN.
The root context path resolved by variant defaults or human-provided root.
The resolved path to the decomposition markdown document.
The _ScopeChange folder under the context root.
A boolean option defaulting to false so stable IDs are preserved unless the human approves renumbering.
The approved write scope for propagation, either variant-default or explicitly narrowed by the human.
The instruction layer governing sequencing and interaction rules.
The instruction layer governing validity and pass-fail requirements.
The instruction layer defining artifacts and schemas.
The instruction layer governing interpretation when ambiguity remains.
The invariant that SCOPE_CHANGE processes only requests originating from the human.
The invariant that decomposition truth and approved metadata changes require explicit human approval at defined gates.
The invariant that removed entities are retired or legacy-annotated rather than silently erased.
The invariant that SCOPE_CHANGE does not directly modify downstream truth such as four-doc sets, Dependencies.csv, estimates, schedules, or generated knowledge artifacts.
The rule that domain-documents is the only writer of active DOMAIN KTY Scoping.md and KA-*.md factual content.
The rule requiring sibling _MEMORY.md or MEMORY.md to be read whenever a local _STATUS.md is read.
The rule excluding .Archive/ folders from downstream scanners, allowlists, section maps, publication inputs, and regeneration inputs unless used for historical audit.
Existing IDs that are never reused for different entities; removed IDs remain reserved.
The requirement that parent entity structural changes resolve all child entities and authoritative ledger bindings in the same amendment.
A binding in Supersession_Delta.csv connecting an SCA decision to a superseded upstream authority fact.
An override type where the prior authority fact is overridden and replacement value governs.
An override type where SCOPE_CHANGE adds detail without contradicting the prior authority.
The requirement that each amendment produces a new snapshot folder and never overwrites prior snapshots.
An action type that creates a new entity or authoritative row in the decomposition.
An action type that retires an existing entity non-destructively.
An action type that changes attributes, descriptions, schemas, notes, or non-lineage mappings of an existing entity.
An action type that moves an existing entity to a different parent while preserving stable identity by default.
An action type that combines two or more entities into a successor entity.
An action type that splits one entity into two or more successor entities.
The practice of referencing sections by semantic name and binding them to variant-specific section names.
The DOMAIN binding of the Unit Ledger semantic section.
The DOMAIN binding of the Secondary Entities semantic section.
The DOMAIN binding of the Tertiary Entities semantic section.
The DOMAIN semantic section for canonical terms and synonyms.
The Gate 2 output containing impact summary, derivative package status, derivative surface classification, orphan risk, staleness risk, handoff notes, and rerun recommendations.
The Gate 4 output describing approved propagation within write scope, downstream reruns, derivative classifications, and closure validation lanes.
The machine-readable action register accounting for every atomic change in an amendment.
A per-SCA KTY content action and evidence ledger owned by SCOPE_CHANGE, not a cumulative content-disposition register.
A manifest action assigned deterministically from the approved SCA action and affected KTY-local content need.
A ContentAction used to retire active KTY content while preserving archive evidence.
A ContentAction that dispatches domain-documents with AUTHORITY_MODE SCA_DRIVEN.
A ContentAction for verifying active content, path references, and factual-use gate without rewriting factual content.
A ContentAction requiring an authority basis explaining why no KTY-local content disposition is needed.
A KTY remediation manifest field controlling whether downstream factual use is allowed, regeneration-only, blocked, retired, or not applicable.
A rollup state for SCA-owned KTY content remediation manifest rows.
A state field identifying the highest phase the current artifact state supports.
The cumulative claim-level binding map for all accepted supersession bindings from all prior SCAs.
The snapshot artifact recording all human decisions at each gate.
The snapshot artifact recording closure and downstream ownership state.
The snapshot artifact containing final summary, state fields, rerun recommendations, and CHANGE handoff.
A handoff state field indicating whether main decomposition document amendments are incomplete or complete.
A handoff state field indicating whether affected decomposition-local derivative surfaces are in parity.
A handoff state field indicating whether downstream reruns are pending or complete.
A handoff state field indicating whether post-regeneration metadata alignment is complete.
A handoff state field indicating the current audit or verification state.
